methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OBSIDIA Semiconductor is a seed-stage company in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The comparable universe consists of 11 same-sector peers: 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent. However, the peer-median method is not applicable here. The narrow peer set for seed-stage semiconductor companies yields fewer than three comparable datapoints when filtered by stage, adjacent-stage positioning, and valuation tier. Applying an all-sector median would introduce significant methodological bias given the heterogeneity of business models, go-to-market strategies, and capital intensity across the semiconductor landscape.

Without sufficient narrow-stage comparable data, traditional triangulation methods cannot be reliably deployed. A credible valuation would require alternative approaches such as first-principles technology risk assessment, customer traction milestones, or founder track record analysis—none of which are present in the available dataset. The broader public comps (NVIDIA, AMD, Mobileye) and private peers operate at vastly different scales and development stages, making direct revenue multiples or EV/chip-equivalent metrics inappropriate for a seed-stage entity.

No valuation range can be responsibly synthesized from the data provided. The key uncertainty is the absence of observable seed-stage semiconductor transactions or current funding metrics that would anchor an estimate. Further due diligence on OBSIDIA's IP defensibility, technical milestones, and capital requirements is required before valuation.
